descriptionHtml:
Bug B19 · excluded (All tickets still in progress / ready for PR (not counted, Quinn 2026-10-14)) · was P1

Retention / purge is not implemented per UAT 3.6: 13-hour Important Points and 37-hour tasks, handoffs and vitals are still there; nothing is purged unless a device opens the app; past 500 patients some charts are skipped

Tickets: TFA-94699 in progress · counts as a QA bug: no (ticket in progress) · found on: local

Note: One root cause behind 19 cases; the windows themselves are decision D6

Other cases of the same bug (counted once): OAT-04/S01, OAT-04/S04, OAT-04/S07, OAT-04/S08, OAT-04/S11, OAT-04/S15, OAT-04/S17, OAT-04/S23, OAT-04/S24, OAT-04/S26, OAT-04/S27, TC-10/S21, TC-11/S25, TC-12/S05, TC-13/S15, TC-13/S16, TC-12/S29, TC-13/S29

Approach · OAT-04 Data Retention · S14 Purge with no page of that mode open: app closed, signed out, or working only in the other mode

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • T2 The purge runs on the server: records clear at their window whether or not any device has the app open. (TFA-94699 AC 7; UAT 3.7 (retention claim)) — gate: blocked: TFA-94699 in progress
  • U11 Live patient data never survives past its window: once an item clears, no copy of it remains anywhere live (other fields of the chart, dated histories, the patient-list row, handoffs, drafts). … (UAT OAT-04 Expected 2; UAT 3.7 (retention claim)) — gate: blocked: TFA-94699 in progress
  • U10 Records clear exactly at their window: each item is still present just before its window ends and gone just after it. (UAT OAT-04 Expected 1; TFA-94699 AC 1) — gate: blocked: TFA-94699 in progress
  • U9 Nursing Home keeps the last two visits: notes, transcripts and medication events from older visits are deleted; the chronic medication list and open tasks persist until changed; … (UAT OAT-04 (B); UAT 3.6 (Nursing Home: pre-round 12 h, encounter 12 h, note 18 h, last two visits); UAT 3.3; TFA-94699 AC 1 (Nursing Home line)) — gate: blocked: TFA-94699 in progress

Test design technique: State transition (state-transition) — Go through the steps in order (add → edit → delete, day 1 → day 2, offline → online) and check the state after each step.

Given Four fresh physicians. A, B and C each have one Hospital patient whose vitals, labs, an active row and an open task are aged to 37 h: A has no session open, B has signed out, C is signed in with only the Nursing Home list open. …

When Wait the agreed purge lag (Q1) after the window with no page of the affected mode open, then read the raw documents

Then A, B and C: the aged Hospital items are deleted, the same as for a physician who opened the Hospital list. D: the visits older than the last two are gone

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): TFA-94699 AC 7 ('the purge runs on the server'), the 3.7 retention claim and 3.3 / U9: aged data still present for A, B or C, or a visit older than the last two still present for D, after the agreed lag = Fail

Where it ran: local retention (clock moved to check retention); test method API · API (Convex functions); lane planned in the matrix: manual (blocked)

S14 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/OAT-04.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row.

Issue type: Known product issue · environment local · tickets TFA-94699 in progress

If the physician is signed out, has not opened the app, or works only in the other care setting, nothing is purged: 37 h-old vitals, labs and medication rows, and Nursing Home visits older than the last two, stay indefinitely.

Evidence: allure 22916e08-…-result.json; retention lane. 0 checks pass, 5 fail, all known K12: the purge is a client-called mutation and crons.ts has only the session sweep. Control: running the client's own applyLifecycle removes the Hospital items. Q1 (acceptable lag) is recorded.

Environment: local — main e02167f, local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane retention.

Test method: API · API (Convex functions); secondary: CODEREVIEW · Code review — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: retention.

UAT item: OAT-04 Data Retention · Section: B · Operational Acceptance Tests · Scenario: OAT-04/S14

Purge with no page of that mode open: app closed, signed out, or working only in the other mode

Tickets: TFA-94699 Data Retention & Purge (in progress)

New local lane retention: status failed in retention/results.json → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue)).

How it is tested (retention/plan.json, automatable: yes): Browser + API: physicians A (session never used again), B (signed out through Better Auth), C (browser open on /snf only), D (NH resident with 4 visits, browser open on /rounding only); items aged 37 h; run the app's cron (sessions:_sweep), keep the pages open 3 minutes, raw rows read by admin without any client purge call. Traces are off in retention.config.ts (a trace holds JWTs and the session cookie); the first run's trace.zip was deleted. — Q1 lag is undecided, but main has no server job at all, so any lag gives the same answer; recorded with the lag used.

Where it ran: local

No client purge call was made by the runner. The agreed lag is Q1; main has no server-side purge job (convex/crons.ts), so a longer wait cannot change the outcome. | control: after A's own rounding:applyLifecycle the aged vitals/labs/row are gone | control: after D's own snf:applyLifecycle visit D1 is still present (main keeps 3 visits, K7) — setup/read calls retried on the local 1 s limit: 1

Product issue: If the physician is signed out, has not opened the app, or works only in the other care setting, nothing is purged: 37 h-old vitals, labs and medication rows (Hospital) and visits older than the last two (Nursing Home) stay on the chart indefinitely. Breaks TFA-94699 AC 7 ('the purge runs on the server') and the UAT 3.7 retention claim. Known in the matrix: K12.

Evidence: 1 attached; 1 not attached:

  • retention/artifacts-run1/oat04-ui-OAT-04-S14-purge--74ad3-or-only-the-other-mode-open — a folder (3 items), not attached

Dev run: skipped: local-only — local-only — Needs the aging helper (a test-only internal mutation that moves a chart's stamps back, called with the local stack's admin key) and the retention-db runner, which seeds through e2e/support/backend.ts and reads the raw rows with adminQuery; dev has no admin key and the dev runner calls only the l…. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
